title: Two Brain Pathways Initiate Distinct Forward Walking Programs in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results 'A neural activation screen identifies candidate walking initiation neurons'; Fig. 1A-F; Fig. S1; Videos S1-S2
quote: SS01540 activation elicited forward walking with a strong turning component whereas SS01587 activation induced straight forward walking
mapping_basis: Paper: SS01540 'labels DNp09 (henceforth referred to as P9) (Namiki et al., 2018)'; kit lists the name DNp09 as ambiguous (also hemibrain name of DNp71) and SS01540 as AMBIGUOUS DNp09;DNp71; Namiki nomenclature supports MANC DNp09.
stimulation: Screen: continuous white light 0.5 mW/cm2 for 7 min; retest: 630 nm ~4.5 mW/cm2 pulsed 50 Hz (5 ms), 30 s ON x3 (grooming assay) or 10 s ON x3 (copulation assay)
type_coverage: a pair of ipsilateral DNs (one cell per hemisphere)
sensory_condition: bowl-shaped arena; powdered (grooming) flies or females mid-copulation; transient assays in the dark with IR backlight
other_cell_types: a few additional neurons (Figures S2A, S2B)
mushroom body gamma lobe neurites (SS01540 only, Fig. S2G)
penetrance: reliably initiated walking in powdered (grooming) flies and in copulating females
n_flies_note: screen n=12-16 per genotype per condition; grooming retest n=16-24 flies/genotype; copulation n=9-11 flies/genotype
notes: Walking initiated from non-walking states (grooming, copulation), so all leg pairs are coded yes under the walking convention. Centroid tracking only (FlyTracker), no leg tracking. The screen (Fig. 1A-B) and the acute retests (Fig. 1C-F) are coded as one Fig. 1 experiment because they have the same outcome. Figure images are not in the room.

title: Speed dependent descending control of freezing behavior in Drosophila melanogaster.
source_locator: Results 'Activation of DNp09 neurons induced freezing' and 'Freezing probability upon DNp09 activation depended on speed'; Fig. 6b-g; Supplementary Movie 4; Methods 'Optogenetic activation'
quote: We found that CsChrimson activation of DNp09 neurons was sufficient to trigger freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of trials
mapping_basis: Paper uses the Namiki name DNp09 with split line SS1540 (SS01540); kit marks the name DNp09 as ambiguous (also hemibrain DNp71) and SS01540 as AMBIGUOUS DNp09;DNp71; Namiki name and line support MANC DNp09.
stimulation: 627 nm LEDs, 0.025 mW/mm2, 10 x (2 s ON / 20 s OFF); closed loop: 2 s pulses triggered at low (<1 mm), high (>7.5 mm) or very high (>10 mm displacement per 500 ms) speeds
sensory_condition: freely moving in 30 mm (open loop) or 60 mm (closed loop) arenas, IR backlight; controls raised without retinal
other_cell_types: weak off-target labeling (unnamed; FlyLight page for SS01540)
penetrance: freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of stimulations; closed loop 85% (506/593) at low speed vs 55% (223/403) at very high speed
n_flies_note: 80 retinal-fed test flies, 72 controls (open loop); 50 flies per speed condition (closed loop)
notes: Main outcome is freezing (immobility classified from pixel change; no leg tracking), so legs are no and the effect is stops. Fig. 6d: baseline ~10 mm/s (flies mostly already walking); a brief speed spike at light onset ('DNp09-induced freezing was always preceded by running') then freezing. In stimulations without freezing, speed stayed raised (~15 mm/s). The running burst is a speed change in walking flies, listed only as secondary. Jumps at light offset. The closed-loop speed conditions differ only in freezing probability, so they are not split.

These are firing-rate predictions, not a rhythm score, rank or driver call, and are not used as evidence.
